subject: Model sourcing & update-notification plan — Acme Health RFP
messages:
From: RFP Coordinator <rfp@acmehealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: model sourcing attestation + update notifications (Acme Health RFP)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for engaging with Acme Health on the RFP. As part of our security and procurement review we need a short attestation and operational description covering:

- How Redwood tracks model provenance (source checkpoints, weights, training data attestations).
- Which open-model licenses you knowingly host or make available via the Redwood Catalog (examples: Apache 2.0, MIT, GPLv3, CC-BY).
- Your policy for models that contain copyleft or otherwise restrictive licenses (distribution/hosting constraints).
- Version pinning and automatic updates: how customers are notified of updates, and whether updates are opt-in or auto-applied.

Could you provide a single-page summary plus a licensing matrix and any attachments by EOD Friday? We will include your responses in the procurement packet and circulate to legal.

Appreciate a point of contact and any drive links/documents you can share.

Best,
Samir (on behalf of Acme RFP team)
Samir Patel
RFP Coordinator — Acme Health Systems
rfp@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Request: model sourcing attestation + update notifications (Acme Health RFP)

Hi Samir,

Thanks — we can meet the Friday timeline. I'll attach our initial "Model Catalog & Licensing Matrix" and a short update-notification plan; Marcus (product) and Neha (security/compliance) are looped in for any technical/legal clarifications.

High-level notes up front:
- We maintain a catalog with explicit license metadata at the model-asset level and surface an SPDX-like license field in the API.
- For copyleft-licensed weight files (e.g., GPL variants) we do not include those in the hosted Redwood Catalog by default; we can enable them for private deployments at customer request with clear distribution constraints.
- Customers can pin to immutable model-version IDs; automatic updates are opt-in with configurable rollout windows and canary testing. We also provide webhook notifications and change logs for model updates.

Attachments: redwood_model_catalog_licensing_matrix_v1.2.pdf (initial answers), acme_rfp_attachment_answers.csv

I'll follow up with a consolidated email tomorrow after internal confirmation on one license edge-case.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Request: model sourcing attestation + update notifications (internal)

Stephanie / Neha — quick note on the GPL / strong copyleft question Samir raised in item 3.

TL;DR proposal for the matrix answer:
- Hosted Catalog: we only list and serve models whose distribution terms permit cloud hosting (Apache/MIT/BSD/CC-BY-like). GPLv2/3 and other viral copyleft weights are marked as "restricted" and excluded from hosted endpoints. We do however allow distribution of model interfaces and code under GPL where applicable (e.g., model wrappers) as long as the weight file license permits it.
- Private Deployments: for Dedicated/Private customers, we can support hosting of GPL-licensed weights but require customer confirmation and an internal operational checklist (legal signoff, DPA addendum, and explicit distribution controls).

On version pinning: ensure matrix says we expose a stable model_version_id (immutable), and we offer two update modes: manual pin change by the customer or optional auto-update with canary + rollback. If auto-update is enabled, customers receive a 14-day pre-notification by default and a webhook. For critical security fixes we accelerate to a 72-hour notice and a mandatory patch window.

If OK I can draft two short canned lines for the external reply that simplify this for procurement/legal.

— Marcus
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Hi Samir / Bethany,

Thanks for the request and for clarifying the review timeline. Attached is the consolidated Model Catalog & Licensing Matrix (v1.2) and a single-page summary for procurement/legal. Highlights below so you can paste into the packet: 

1) Licensing categories we track (catalog level):
   - Permissive: Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD — included in hosted catalog and served via hosted endpoints.
   - Non-permissive / Special: CC-NC, custom non-commercial — listed with usage flags; require customer review.
   - Copyleft / Viral: GPL-family, AGPL — by default excluded from Redwood hosted endpoints and marked "restricted" in the catalog. Supported for Dedicated/Private deployments with customer consent and legal/ops checklist.

2) Provenance artifacts we provide per model asset:
   - Model manifest (commit hash, checkpoint URI, training-date),
   - SBOM-style weight checksum + storage location,
   - Source-code repository URL + release tag,
   - Training-data provenance statement (where available) and any available dataset licenses.

3) Version pinning & rollout policy:
   - Immutable model_version_id: customers may pin to an immutable identifier.
   - Auto-update opt-in: customers may enable automatic updates; default behaviour is "opt-out" to avoid surprise changes.
   - Update cadence: non-critical updates: 14-day pre-notification + webhook + changelog entry; critical security updates: 72-hour notice and accelerated patching.
   - Rollouts: canary with configurable percentage, automatic rollback on regression/error thresholds.

4) Update-notification channels:
   - Email + tenant admin dashboard alert,
   - Webhook payload with change details,
   - Changelog entry and Drive link to the full release notes.

5) Copyleft / redistribution handling:
   - We will not serve GPL/AGPL weight binaries from our hosted tier unless explicit legal review and a signed addendum is in place. For Private or Dedicated, we can host with additional controls and a written customer confirmation that they accept redistribution constraints.

Attachments included: redwood_model_catalog_licensing_matrix_v1.2.pdf (detailed per-model rows and license flags), acme_rfp_attachment_answers.csv (quick Q&A table).
